data.why: 12 of Apple's 13 Walmart rows are already Grocery and the 13th is identical; Discover and Capital One both file the same store under Merchandise. Covers WALMART SUPERCENTER and WALMART STORE 03118.
Capital One writes the same store with a space — $508 across 6 rows that would otherwise miss the WALMART needle entirely.
The abbreviation Apple uses on returns. Without it the −$315.88 and −$273.90 refunds net against Misc instead of against the Groceries they came out of.
$1,054 across 18 rows. Already Grocery on Apple; the rule makes it independent of which card it lands on next.
Grocery, every issuer, every row.
The literal string on the statement is WHOLEFDS DCT 10687 — not `Whole Foods`, which is why the needle is spelled the way the issuer spells it.
Three different tails (MARKET / MARK / MARKET DECATUR) across three issuers: Discover says Supermarkets, Capital One says Merchandise, Citi says nothing. Needle stops before the tail.

The one rule in this file that HAS to be a regex, and the dry run is what found it: `contains ALDI` matches EU KALDIS — Kaldi's Coffee — and quietly moved 44 Food rows into Groceries. A leading word boundary keeps ALDI INC and a future ALDI 54321 while excluding KALDIS. Capital One files the real Aldi rows as Merchandise.
Korean grocery.
Chicago grocery; the apostrophe normalizes to a space.
Citi's two rows ($24.92) are Misc for want of a category column. Store numbers are kept in the ledger's merchant string, so the needle has to be the stem.
Citi: 10148 CAVA DECATUR, three rows, uncategorized.
Citi Square charge, restaurant. `SQ ` prefix kept so the needle can't collide with the word pisces elsewhere.
Citi, uncategorized; matches both the Square and the direct row.
Already Food on Apple's 8 rows; Citi's row was Misc. One rule makes the card irrelevant.
Citi writes 5GUYS 0539 ECOMM SANDY SPRINGS GA — digits are retained by normalization, so the needle starts with one.
Apple's 13 rows are Entertainment→Fun; Citi's two are Misc. Short needle, checked against the whole corpus: nothing else contains AMC.
Games, filed as Other by Apple.
Music purchases, filed as Other.
A streaming app Discover files under Merchandise.
Audiobook subscription; Other on Apple, Other Services on Capital One.

The $15.89 monthly membership, not a purchase — and the longest-match tier is what keeps it out of the way of any future broad AMAZON rule. Fun rather than Bill because it is cancellable and mostly video; argue with it here rather than per row.
iCloud/Apple One, $9.99 monthly. Needle deliberately not `APPLE` — see the caution in `note`.
App Store / media billing, filed as Merchandise by Discover.
Covers LA FITNESS, LA FITNS DECATUR CHU and LA FITNESS ANNUALFEE. A gym membership is discretionary; this keeps the annual fee with the monthly dues.
A cancellable discount membership, not a ride: Apple filed it Transportation and Discover filed it Entertainment. Named longer than UBER TRIP so precedence is unambiguous either way.
The inconsistency that most needed a rule: 41 rows Transportation (Apple, Capital One) against 12 rows Fun (Discover calls it Travel/ Entertainment), same merchant, $843 total.
Stated explicitly rather than left to the issuer, so that `UBER TRIP` and `UBER EATS` are two decisions on the record and nobody is ever tempted to write one broad UBER rule.
Discover filed its two rows under Travel/ Entertainment→Fun. A ride is a ride.

$506 across 20 rows averaging $25, plus TESLA SERVICE and TESLA SUPERCHARGER — charging and servicing a car, filed as Other by Apple and uncategorized by Capital One. Covers SUPERCHARGER through the stem.
Capital One drops the brand (SUPERCHARGER US), so the TESLA needle alone misses it.
One needle covers EMPIRE PARKING SERVICE, GLOBALAIRPORT PARKING, LAZ PARKING, PEAKPARKING COM and GSU PARKING DECK. Note it is PARKING and not PARK: `BAR TACO INMAN PARK` is dinner.
Campus deck; no PARKING in the string.
Hospital parking deck; needle is long enough not to catch the word park.
PSPT SPATL PRK — a parking operator that abbreviates past any readable needle.
Tires and service, $271, filed Other.
Auto parts and service, filed Other.
Roadside assistance, filed Other.
WHITECAP CAR WASH, filed Other.
A court-payment processor; Apple itself calls one of the two rows Govt-services-parking and the other Other. Same merchant, so one answer.
USO LGBS I66 EXPRESS L — I-66 express lane tolls, $229, filed Other.
Home warranty, $440 across 6 rows Apple already maps (Insurance→Bill) — but its −$125 credit row came through as Misc, so the refund was netting against the wrong category.

7 rows split 4 Bill (Apple: Utilities) / 3 Misc (Apple: Other) for storage and YouTube Premium. Following the issuer's own majority rather than my taxonomy; a subscription that is also a utility is a coin flip and consistency is the point.

$935 across 5 rows, ~$199 every month: a recurring prescription subscription. A standing monthly obligation reads wrong in a discretionary catch-all, and with no health category available Bill is the honest home.
Developer tooling subscription, $15/mo, filed Merchandise.
Software licence, $142, filed Services.
ChatGPT subscription, filed Merchandise.
Covers INTUIT INC (already Bill) and INTUIT TURBOTAX (Misc) — tax filing, once a year, not discretionary.

$2,398 — the single largest Misc line in the ledger. GA STATE UNIV PAYPATH and TN GA STATE UNIV PAYPA are tuition payments; Apple files both as Other. There is no education category, and Bill is where a fixed, non-negotiable obligation belongs. Deliberately does not match GSU PARKING DECK, which is parking.

An issuer reward, not a refund of anything. Left in Misc it nets against Misc spending, making a quarter of the ledger read lower than it was. `Adjustment` is already in the CSP's exclude set, which is the correct treatment of a card artifact (decision #21).
Discover's recurring rewards credit — $31 across 8 rows, same reasoning as Daily Cash.
Discover, $85 redeemed to the statement.
Capital One's redemption row, which it labels Payment/Credit.
Capital One, $34 across 2 rows.
A $2.50 promotional credit on both Rajna's cards; an offer, not a transport refund.
$315 of tours and excursions that Apple files under Hotels→Misc. Delta's flights are already Transportation (Airlines), so this is the activity half of the same trip, not travel logistics.
GEORGIA SPA LAND SAU — a day spa, filed Other. Leisure, not healthcare: nothing here is prescribed.
$306 on one row where the same merchant arrives with the spaces already gone, so the SPA LAND needle misses it. Two spellings of one merchant is two rules — matching 'SPA' alone would be far worse.
